# Tackle Content Style Guide

Source: [General guidelines](https://appdirect.jira.com/wiki/spaces/PC/pages/5727191774/General+guidelines) (Confluence)

## Voice and Tone

- Friendly, contextual, informative — but clean, clear, and concise.
- Show the best way to complete a task. Empower users to be self-sufficient.
- Convey professionalism while being conversational.

### Rules

1. **Active voice, present tense.** Address the user directly as "you."
2. **Never use** "we", "they", or passive constructions when asking users to act.
3. **Be factual and causative.** Never predict the value of the user's experience — avoid "easier", "better", "faster", "more user-friendly."
4. **Be direct.** Prefer imperative mood for instructions.

| Do                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create an offer                                                          | Creating an offer (as a title)                                                                              |
| Your billing is adjusted as your GMV increases.                          | The bill we send will be adjusted as your GMV increases.                                                    |
| Complete all fields.                                                     | It is recommended you complete all fields.                                                                  |
| The offers feature reduces time-to-completion by removing an extra step. | This great new feature has a time-saving component that will make your offers experience faster and easier. |

## Punctuation

| Rule             | Detail                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Oxford comma** | Always use the serial comma: "AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft."                             |
| **No ampersand** | Spell out "and" in all UI copy. Exception only if space is critically limited (status bars). |
| **Periods**      | Apply to full sentences. Do not add periods to fragments, labels, or short list items.       |

## Capitalization and Casing

- **Sentence case** for all headings and subheadings.
- **Tackle feature names:**
  - Title case for the proper noun form: "Tackle Offers", "Tackle Co-Sell", "Tackle Prospect."
  - Lowercase for verb/noun usage in running text: "co-sell an opportunity", "create an offer."
  - In documentation: full name at first mention ("Tackle Offers"), then the UI name alone ("Offers").
- **Third-party names:** follow their official casing exactly — "CloudFormation template", "Salesforce admin", "Google Cloud Console."
- **File extensions:** CAPS when generic ("Upload a CSV"), lowercase when part of a filename ("report.csv").

## UI Label Formatting

| Style         | Use for                                                                            | Examples                                                                |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Bold**      | Interactive elements: buttons, tabs, toggles, links the user clicks                | Click **Save**. Use **Setup** to go to **Object Manager**.              |
| _Italics_     | Static labels: page names, modal names, column headers, field names, status values | In the _Flow_ field, enter the name.                                    |
| `Inline code` | Code values, commands, API names, config keys                                      | Use the `settings.css` file. Replace `example` with your server number. |

Only style the word, not surrounding punctuation (unless punctuation is part of the element).

## Action Verbs for UI

| Verb          | When to use                                                                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **click**     | Buttons, navigation targets, links. Includes "right-click", "double-click", "drag and drop."         |
| **select**    | Radio buttons, dropdowns, checkboxes, multi-selects — the mental action of choosing between options. |
| **create**    | Making something from scratch. Not "add" (which implies referencing something existing).             |
| **remove**    | Soft / undoable delete from the UI.                                                                  |
| **delete**    | Permanent, irreversible removal.                                                                     |
| **configure** | More specific than "set up" — for permissions, settings, integration details.                        |
| **connect**   | Establishing a data flow or human connection (e.g., between Tackle and a marketplace).               |
| **set up**    | General assembly steps toward a broader goal. Verb: "set up"; noun/adjective: "setup."               |

Never write "click on" — just "click."

## Abbreviations and Acronyms

1. **Spell out on first use** with acronym in parentheses: "customer relationship management (CRM) tool."
2. Second mention may use the acronym alone, sparingly.
3. **No Latin abbreviations.** Use "for example" not "e.g.", "that is" not "i.e."
4. **No shortened words** in copy — "organization" not "org", "administrator" not "admin", "application" not "app" — unless part of an official name (e.g., "Storage Admin" role in Google Cloud).
5. **Plural acronyms:** lowercase s, no apostrophe — "ABOs" not "ABO's."
6. **Article matches spoken form:** "an SDDS" not "a SDDS."

## Numbers, Dates, and Times

| Rule                                                                 | Example                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Spell out zero through nine; numerals for 10+                        | "three offers", "12 opportunities" |
| Date format: Month DD, YYYY                                          | "June 6, 2023"                     |
| Abbreviated date (space-constrained): first three letters, no period | "Jun 6, 2023"                      |
| Never use MM/DD/YYYY                                                 | Avoids confusion with DD/MM/YYYY   |

See the [Microsoft Style Guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/numbers) for edge cases.

## Lists

### Numbered lists

Only for ordered steps, priority, or chronological sequences.

### Bulleted lists

For unordered items or multiple options for completing a sentence.

**Sentence-completing bullets** (stem ends with a colon):

- Start each bullet with a capital letter.
- Read each as a standalone sentence.
- End each with a period.

**Simple item lists** (no stem sentence):

- Capitalize first letter
- No periods
- Keep items short (7 words or fewer)

## Links

- Use descriptive link text — the name of the target content, not "click here" or "learn more."
- If a link navigates away from the current context (e.g., app to docs, docs to third-party), add the OpenNew icon after the link.
- Link to third-party documentation for standard tasks rather than rewriting their instructions.

| Do                                                                                                                          | Don't                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Create a service account](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-managing-service-accounts) and include these roles... | If you don't have all the [requirements](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-managing-service-accounts), you won't be able to continue. |

## Sample Content and Placeholders

- The ISV is always "you" / "your" / "your company."
- Example domains: `example.com` only (not .net or .org).
- Example emails: `email@example.com`.
- PascalCase for multi-word placeholder names: "YourCompanyName", "BuyerCompanyName."
- For code samples requiring replacement, call out specific instructions about the replaceable segment in monospace.

## "Please"

Only use "please" when asking users to go beyond standard instructions:

- Do: "Please log out and log in again to reboot the system after the update."
- Don't: "Please enter your email address."

## Terminology

For the approved glossary of Tackle terms, cloud marketplace names, co-sell vocabulary, and the Tackle Way cross-cloud mapping, see [words-and-terms.md](words-and-terms.md).

Key rules:

- "co-sell opportunity" not "deal", "referral", or "co-sell record."
- "accept" (receipt) vs. "approve" (judgment) — use precisely.
- "decline" not "reject."
- "cloud marketplace" (lowercase) when general; proper name when specific ("AWS Marketplace").
- "cloud provider" never shortened to "cloud."
- "sign in / sign out" not "log in / log out."
- "left menu" not "left nav."
- "Tackle Support" (proper noun) for all support references.
- Always alphabetize cloud marketplaces in a series: AWS, Google Cloud Marketplace, Microsoft commercial marketplace.

## Validation Checklist

Before returning any UI copy, verify:

- [ ] Active voice, present tense, direct "you" address
- [ ] No passive constructions, no "we"/"they"
- [ ] No value predictions ("easier", "better", "faster")
- [ ] Oxford comma used in all series
- [ ] No ampersand — "and" spelled out
- [ ] Sentence case for headings
- [ ] Tackle feature names cased correctly (title case proper noun, lowercase verb form)
- [ ] Third-party names match their official casing
- [ ] Correct action verbs (click/select/create/remove/delete)
- [ ] Abbreviations spelled out on first use; no Latin abbreviations
- [ ] Dates in "Month DD, YYYY" format
- [ ] Terms match the approved glossary (see [words-and-terms.md](words-and-terms.md))
- [ ] "sign in" not "log in"; "left menu" not "left nav"
- [ ] "please" only for beyond-standard requests
